ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A > \angle B$, the $\triangle ABC$ is first folded along the crease $CE$ so that point $A$ can fall on $BC$. After flattening, $\angle B$ is folded along the crease $GF$ making point $B$ coincide with point $A$, where $FG$ intersects sides $BC$ and $AB$ at points $F$ and $G$, respectively. $CD$ is the height from the hypotenuse. If $\angle DCE = \angle B$, then what is $\frac{BF}{CE}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $AF$, \\
$\because$ when $\triangle ABC$ is folded for the first time along crease $CE$, making point $A$ fall onto $BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACE=\angle BCE=45^\circ$, \\
$\because$ by folding $\angle B$ along crease $GF$, making point $B$ coincide with point $A$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle FAB$, $FA=FB$, \\
$\because$ $\angle ACD+\angle DCB=\angle B+\angle DCB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD=\angle B$, \\
$\because$ $\angle DCE=\angle B$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD=\angle DCE=\angle B=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACE=22.5^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AFC=\angle B+\angle FAB=2\angle B=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ AFC is an isosceles right triangle, \\
Let $AC=CF=a$, then $AF=\sqrt{a^2+a^2}=\sqrt{2}a$, \\
$\because$ $\angle CAB=90^\circ-\angle B=67.5^\circ$, $\angle CEA=\angle B+\angle BCE=67.5^\circ$, \\
that is $\angle CAE=\angle CEA$, \\
$\therefore$ CA=CE, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BF}{CE}=\frac{AF}{CA}=\frac{\sqrt{2}a}{a}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a right triangle ABC, A, D, E, G, B are successively located on the base AB, and C is above and to the left. Sides AC and CB intersect at C, and the problem statement indicates ∠ACB=90°. CD goes from C perpendicular to the base AB, intersecting at D. The dashed line CE connects from C to E on the base, and is the first crease. The dashed line GF connects from G on the base to F on side CB, and is the second crease; F is located on CB, and G is located on AB. Reasoning: The first folding along CE makes A fall on BC, and C is on the crease and does not move, so ray CA is reflected to the direction along CB, and CE bisects the right angle ∠ACB. Therefore ∠ACE=∠ECB=45°. Since CD is the altitude on the hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC, therefore ∠ACD=∠B. It is also known that ∠DCE=∠B, and the order at point C in the figure is CA, CD, CE, CB, so ∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2∠B. Thus 45°=2∠B, obtaining ∠B=22.5°, ∠A=67.5°. The second folding along GF makes B coincide with A, so point F on the crease satisfies FA=FB. Also F is on CB, therefore ∠ABF=∠B; in isosceles triangle AFB, ∠FAB=∠ABF=∠B. Because FC and FB are opposite rays on the same straight line, the exterior angle ∠AFC=∠FAB+∠ABF=2∠B=45°. Also AC⊥CB, and F is on CB, so ∠ACF=90°, hence △ACF is a 45°-45°-90° isosceles right triangle, AF=√2·AC. Next look at △ACE: ∠CAE=∠CAB=67.5°; also the angle between CE and CB is 45°, and the angle between AB and CB is ∠B=22.5°, so ∠CEA=45°+22.5°=67.5°. Therefore ∠CAE=∠CEA, obtaining CE=AC. Finally, from folding, BF=AF, so BF/CE=AF/AC=√2.

method.method_draft: Synthetic angle-chase route. First read the figure as a right triangle with A,D,E,G,B on the bottom side in that order, C above, CD drawn to AB, CE the first crease meeting AB at E, and GF the second crease meeting BC at F and AB at G. From the first fold, reflection sends CA onto a segment along CB, so CE bisects the right angle at C; hence ∠ACE=∠ECB=45°. From the altitude CD to hypotenuse AB in a right triangle, use ∠ACD=∠B. The given ∠DCE=∠B and the visual order A-C-D-E-B around angle C give ∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2∠B, so ∠B=22.5°. For the second fold, since B is reflected to A across GF, any point on the crease is equidistant from A and B; in particular F satisfies FA=FB, and the angle at A made by AF with AB equals ∠B. Thus in isosceles triangle AFB, the exterior angle ∠AFC along FC is 2∠B=45°. Since FC lies on CB and AC⊥CB, triangle ACF is a 45-45-90 triangle, giving AF=sqrt(2)·AC. Finally, in triangle ACE, ∠CAE=∠A=67.5° and ∠CEA=67.5° because CE makes 45° with CB and AB makes angle B with CB; hence CE=AC. Since BF=AF from the fold, BF/CE=sqrt(2).

图像描述：图中是一个直角三角形 ABC，A、D、E、G、B 依次位于底边 AB 上，C 在上方偏左。边 AC 与 CB 相交于 C，题设标明 ∠ACB=90°。CD 从 C 垂到底边 AB，交于 D。虚线 CE 从 C 连到底边上的 E，是第一次折痕。虚线 GF 从底边上的 G 连到边 CB 上的 F，是第二次折痕，F 位于 CB 上，G 位于 AB 上。
推理：第一次沿 CE 折叠使 A 落到 BC 上，且 C 在折痕上不动，所以射线 CA 被反射到沿 CB 的方向，CE 平分直角 ∠ACB。因此 ∠ACE=∠ECB=45°。由于 CD 是直角三角形 ABC 斜边 AB 上的高，故 ∠ACD=∠B。又已知 ∠DCE=∠B，并且从图中 C 点处的顺序为 CA、CD、CE、CB，所以 ∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2∠B。于是 45°=2∠B，得到 ∠B=22.5°，∠A=67.5°。第二次沿 GF 折叠使 B 与 A 重合，所以折痕上的点 F 满足 FA=FB。又 F 在 CB 上，因此 ∠ABF=∠B；在等腰三角形 AFB 中，∠FAB=∠ABF=∠B。因为 FC 与 FB 是同一直线上的反向射线，所以外角 ∠AFC=∠FAB+∠ABF=2∠B=45°。又 AC⊥CB，且 F 在 CB 上，所以 ∠ACF=90°，从而 △ACF 是 45°-45°-90° 等腰直角三角形，AF=√2·AC。接着看 △ACE：∠CAE=∠CAB=67.5°；又 CE 与 CB 夹角为 45°，AB 与 CB 夹角为 ∠B=22.5°，所以 ∠CEA=45°+22.5°=67.5°。因此 ∠CAE=∠CEA，得到 CE=AC。最后由折叠得 BF=AF，所以 BF/CE=AF/AC=√2。

method.method_draft: Coordinate/trigonometric route. Read the diagram with AB as the bottom side, C the right-angle vertex, E on AB where the first crease CE meets it, and F on BC where the perpendicular-bisector fold GF meets it. Set coordinates C=(0,0), B=(b,0), A=(0,a), so ∠B=θ and tan θ=a/b. The first fold makes CE the internal bisector of the right angle at C, so CE is the line y=x. The altitude condition gives ∠ACD=θ, and the given ∠DCE=θ; since CD and CE are between CA and CB as drawn, 2θ=∠ACE=45°, so θ=22.5° and a/b=tan22.5°=sqrt(2)-1. Compute E as the intersection of y=x with AB: line AB is y=a-(a/b)x, so E=(ab/(a+b), ab/(a+b)) and CE=sqrt(2)ab/(a+b). For the second fold, GF maps B to A, hence it is the perpendicular bisector of AB; since F=(x,0) lies on BC and on this crease, impose FA=FB: x^2+a^2=(b-x)^2, giving BF=b-x=(a^2+b^2)/(2b). Substitute r=a/b=sqrt(2)-1 into BF/CE=[b(1+r^2)/2]/[sqrt(2)rb/(1+r)] to obtain sqrt(2).

图像描述：图中是一个直角三角形ABC，A、D、E、G、B大致在下方同一直线AB上，C在上方，∠ACB处标有直角。D是从C向AB作的垂足；虚线CE从C连到AB上的E；虚线GF经过AB上的G并交CB于F，表示第二次折痕；F位于边CB上。

推理：按指定坐标法，把直角顶点C作为原点，令两条直角边分别为坐标轴，取C=(0,0)，B=(b,0)，A=(0,a)。设∠B=θ，则在直角三角形中tanθ=a/b。

第一次折叠沿CE使A落到BC上，由于C在折痕上，射线CA被折到射线CB，所以CE是∠ACB的内角平分线。因为∠ACB=90°，所以CE为直线y=x，且∠ACE=45°。

CD是斜边AB上的高。在直角三角形中，由相似关系可得∠ACD=∠B=θ。题给∠DCE=∠B=θ，并且从图中看CD与CE都在∠ACB内部，且CD位于CA与CE之间，所以∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2θ。于是2θ=45°，θ=22.5°，因此a/b=tan22.5°=√2-1。

求CE：直线AB过A=(0,a)、B=(b,0)，方程为y=a-(a/b)x。CE为y=x，与AB相交于E，所以x=a-(a/b)x，解得x=ab/(a+b)。故E=(ab/(a+b), ab/(a+b))，CE=√2·ab/(a+b)。

第二次折叠沿GF使B与A重合，因此GF是AB的垂直平分线。F在BC上，设F=(x,0)，由FA=FB得x^2+a^2=(b-x)^2，解得BF=b-x=(a^2+b^2)/(2b)。

令r=a/b=√2-1，则BF=b(1+r^2)/2，CE=√2·rb/(1+r)。所以BF/CE=[b(1+r^2)/2]/[√2·rb/(1+r)]=(1+r^2)(1+r)/(2√2r)。代入r=√2-1，化简得BF/CE=√2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A > \angle B$, $\triangle ABC$ is first folded along the crease $CE$ so that point $A$ falls on $BC$. After flattening, $\angle B$ is folded along the crease $GF$, making point $B$ coincide with point $A$, where $FG$ intersects sides $BC$ and $AB$ at points $F$ and $G$, respectively. $CD$ is the altitude to the hypotenuse. If $\angle DCE = \angle B$, then what is $\frac{BF}{CE}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $AF$. 
$\because$ when $\triangle ABC$ is folded for the first time along crease $CE$, making point $A$ fall onto $BC$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle ACE=\angle BCE=45^\circ$. 
$\because$ by folding $\angle B$ along crease $GF$, making point $B$ coincide with point $A$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle FAB$, $FA=FB$. 
$\because$ $\angle ACD+\angle DCB=\angle B+\angle DCB=90^\circ$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD=\angle B$. 
$\because$ $\angle DCE=\angle B$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD=\angle DCE=\angle B=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACE=22.5^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $\angle AFC=\angle B+\angle FAB=2\angle B=45^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ AFC is an isosceles right triangle. 
Let $AC=CF=a$, then $AF=\sqrt{a^2+a^2}=\sqrt{2}a$. 
$\because$ $\angle CAB=90^\circ-\angle B=67.5^\circ$, $\angle CEA=\angle B+\angle BCE=67.5^\circ$, 
that is $\angle CAE=\angle CEA$, 
$\therefore$ $CA=CE$. 
$\therefore$ $\frac{BF}{CE}=\frac{AF}{CA}=\frac{\sqrt{2}a}{a}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.

Sides AC and CB intersect at C, and the problem statement indicates ∠ACB=90°. CD goes from C perpendicular to the base AB, intersecting at D. The dashed line CE connects from C to E on the base, and is the first crease. The dashed line GF connects from G on the base to F on side CB, and is the second crease; F is located on CB, and G is located on AB.
Reasoning: The first folding along CE makes A fall on BC, and C is on the crease and does not move, so ray CA is reflected to the direction along CB, and CE bisects the right angle ∠ACB. Therefore ∠ACE=∠ECB=45°. Since CD is the altitude on the hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC, therefore ∠ACD=∠B. It is also known that ∠DCE=∠B, and the order at point C in the figure is CA, CD, CE, CB, so ∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2∠B. Thus 45°=2∠B, obtaining ∠B=22.5°, ∠A=67.5°. The second folding along GF makes B coincide with A, so point F on the crease satisfies FA=FB. Also F is on CB, therefore ∠ABF=∠B; in isosceles triangle AFB, ∠FAB=∠ABF=∠B. Because FC and FB are opposite rays on the same straight line, the exterior angle ∠AFC=∠FAB+∠ABF=2∠B=45°. Also AC⊥CB, and F is on CB, so ∠ACF=90°, hence △ACF is a 45°-45°-90° isosceles right triangle, AF=√2·AC. Next look at △ACE: ∠CAE=∠CAB=67.5°; also the angle between CE and CB is 45°, and the angle between AB and CB is ∠B=22.5°, so ∠CEA=45°+22.5°=67.5°. Therefore ∠CAE=∠CEA, obtaining CE=AC. Finally, from folding, BF=AF, so BF/CE=AF/AC=√2.

Reasoning: The first folding along CE makes A fall on BC, and C is on the crease and does not move, so ray CA is reflected to the direction along CB, and CE bisects the right angle ∠ACB. Therefore ∠ACE=∠ECB=45°. Since CD is the altitude on the hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC, therefore ∠ACD=∠B. It is also known that ∠DCE=∠B, and the order at point C in the figure is CA, CD, CE, CB, so ∠ACE=∠ACD+∠DCE=2∠B. Thus 45°=2∠B, obtaining ∠B=22.5°, ∠A=67.5°. The second folding along GF makes B coincide with A, so point F on the crease satisfies FA=FB. Also F is on CB, therefore ∠ABF=∠B; in isosceles triangle AFB, ∠FAB=∠ABF=∠B. Because FC and FB are opposite rays on the same straight line, the exterior angle ∠AFC=∠FAB+∠ABF=2∠B=45°. Also AC⊥CB, and F is on CB, so ∠ACF=90°, hence △ACF is a 45°-45°-90° isosceles right triangle, AF=√2·AC. Next look at △ACE: ∠CAE=∠CAB=67.5°; also the angle between CE and CB is 45°, and the angle between AB and CB is ∠B=22.5°, so ∠CEA=45°+22.5°=67.5°. Therefore ∠CAE=∠CEA, obtaining CE=AC. Finally, from folding, BF=AF, so BF/CE=AF/AC=√2.
